status_summary: Executive Order 14154 (published 2025-01-29) revoked Executive Orders 14008 and 14096, among others, and Executive Orders 14151 and 14173 directed agencies to end DEI programs. E&E News reported on 2025-01-24 that DOE was suspending community benefit plan and Justice40 work, and a DOE counsel memorandum dated 2025-02-28 permits removing such terms from pending and future awards. On 2026-02-06 the Fourth Circuit vacated the preliminary injunction that had blocked parts of Executive Orders 14151 and 14173 and remanded the case, which remains pending in district court. On 2026-05-29 OMB proposed a government-wide financial assistance rule, with DOE a participating agency, that would direct agencies to eliminate unlawful DEI mandates and identity-based preferences in grantmaking and would bar unlawful discrimination across the award process. The 2025-11-20 DOE organization chart lists no separate energy justice office.

timeline.event: DOE's acting Secretary told staff DOE was suspending work that requires or enforces community benefit plans and Justice40 requirements and moving to end DEI policies and funding.
In an email that day, DOE shared with OPM a list of 69 DEI-related employees placed on administrative leave, per E&E News reporting.
Executive Order 14154 published; section 4 revokes Executive Orders 14008 and 14096, among others.
Executive Order 14151, ending federal DEI programs and preferencing, published.
Executive Order 14173, on illegal discrimination and merit-based opportunity, published.
Senate Democrats urged the Energy Secretary not to terminate the Office of Energy Justice and Equity, which had staff on leave; the office was reported as at risk, not confirmed terminated.
DOE counsel memorandum, issued in light of a court order, permits removal of community benefit plan, DEI and Justice40 terms from pending and future funding actions.
DOE organization chart lists an Office of Minority Economic Impact and no separate energy justice office.

The Fourth Circuit, in a published opinion in NADOHE v. Trump (No. 25-1189), vacated the preliminary injunction that had blocked three provisions of Executive Orders 14151 and 14173 and remanded the case to the District of Maryland.
timeline.source: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit (opinion copy hosted by Democracy Forward)

timeline.event: OMB published a proposed government-wide federal financial assistance regulation (91 FR 32198) whose preamble says agencies would eliminate unlawful DEI mandates and identity-based preferences in grantmaking and bar unlawful discrimination across the award process, with new sections on disparate-impact theories and discriminatory event services; DOE is a participating agency with conforming changes to 2 CFR parts 901, 902 and 910 (comments closed 2026-07-13).

title: End DOE energy justice, Justice40 and DEI programs
uncertainties: The fair-treatment-of-employees element was not separately checked. The effect of the Fourth Circuit ruling and remand on individual DOE awards was not traced, and the opinion was read through a copy hosted by Democracy Forward, an advocacy group, rather than on the court's own site; the copy carries the Fourth Circuit caption, case number 25-1189, the panel and the court's filing header (Doc. 106, filed 2026-02-06) on each page. The organization chart shows offices at a high level and does not by itself confirm abolition of sub-offices; the DOE organization chart page was marked as updated 2026-08-03 and still listed no energy justice office, but the dated chart file behind that update was not located. The FY2026 Energy and Water appropriations act (Public Law 119-74, 2026-01-23) was reported by CRS not to carry the House-passed ban on DEI funding, and no appropriations language restoring or mandating these programs was found. A Federal Register search of Energy Department documents from 2025-11-20 onward for environmental justice, community benefits plan and DEI terms returned no results. The regulatory text of the OMB proposed rule, including the DOE-specific changes, was not read in full; the description rests on the preamble, which does not mention Justice40 or environmental justice in the portion read.
